newsitem.title: USA: Baker Hughes in pact to acquire Drilex.
newsitem.headline: Baker Hughes in pact to acquire Drilex.

text.p: Baker Hughes Inc said Thursday it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Houston-based Drilex International Inc for the equivalent of either $15 or $16 per share in Baker Hughes stock, depending on the performance of Drilex.
The acquisition is expected to close before the end of Baker Hughes' fiscal year on September 30.

DRLX Partners LP, which owns 61.8 percent of Drilex, has agreed to vote in favor of the deal, and Baker Hughes has an option to buy from DRLX 1.7 million Drilex shares, or 25 percent of total outstanding, at $16 a share.
Drilex has about 6.8 million shares (fully diluted) outstanding.
The market value for Baker Hughes stock in the exchange will be set by the closing prices for 10 trading days ending before the second trading day before the deal is due to close.
Drilex had revenues of $76.1 million and earnings before interest, taxes and depreciation of $13.5 million in 1996, Baker Hughes said.
Drilex said Thursday that for the first quarter it would report revenues of $17 million, break-even net income per share, and cash flow per share of $0.28.
The first quarter data will reflect delays in project starts and lower than expected revenues from Louisiana operations, Drilex said.
Drilex provides products and services used primarily in the directional drilling and workover of oil and gas wells.

"The acquisition of Drilex will increase our exposure to a number of directional drilling opportunities, particularly among U.S. independent producers where Drilex enjoys a fine reputation," said Baker Hughes Chief Executive Max Lukens.
